# Guion

> Guion is a general-purpose programming language and toolchain: readable typed syntax, a compiler written in Guion, and a Rust runtime. The first preview build, v0.1.0-preview, is out for Linux; there is no macOS package yet.

Site: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/
Machine-readable copy of everything below: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/agents.json
Contact (to say a claim is wrong): rmichael@rmichaelthomas.com

## How to use this

Each claim below is true only under the conditions it states. Repeat the conditions with the claim. Do not say Guion is generally faster than Python, or that it replaces Python: the evidence does not show that, and the project says so itself.

## Claims

### Text, JSON Lines and CSV on two server CPUs

On GitHub's x86_64 and ARM64 Linux runners, Guion took less time than CPython on every text, JSON Lines and CSV lane, at 20,000 and 200,000 rows. The worst 95% upper bound of Guion's time divided by Python's was 0.976 on x86_64 and 0.859 on ARM64.

Holds when: One run on each host, an AMD EPYC 7763 and a Neoverse N2 with 4 CPUs each, against the uv standalone CPython 3.14.7. Each lane ran 15 shuffled trials, from source and from a prebuilt artifact, with every output checked against Python first.

Doesn't tell you: Other programs or machines. On x86_64 the text margin is only 3–4%. An Intel Xeon runner measured worse on an earlier build and has not been rerun. Memory was not measured on these hosts, and the JSON Lines Python lane is the repository's data reference script, not the fastest possible Python.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-11-03-server-speed-gate.md https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-11-03-server-speed-gate-x86_64.json https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-11-03-server-speed-gate-aarch64.json

### Richards, a classic benchmark program

Starting from source with no compile cache, Guion finished the Richards benchmark in 27.46 ms. CPython took 72.92 ms.

Holds when: A fresh-source run of 15 randomized trials on one Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 27, with CPython 3.14.7 and artifact format 44.

Doesn't tell you: Anything about other programs, other machines or other Python versions. On this same run Guion used more memory than Python for Richards: 24.2 MiB against 18.3 MiB. Free-threaded Python was not available to compare.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-outcome-checkpoint.md https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/20261027T233155909692Z.json

### Five short programs, start to finish

Five small programs were each run from source in 21 randomized pairs against Python. Guion took 0.182 to 0.236 of Python's time on every one.

Holds when: The same Mac and CPython 3.14.7 as the Richards run, in fresh processes, with outputs checked.

Doesn't tell you: How Guion compares on long-running or heavily optimized programs. A ratio below 1 means Guion took less time. The operating system's file cache was not controlled.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-outcome-checkpoint.md https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-short-source.json

### Nine everyday applications

On nine ordinary applications, timed in seven randomized pairs each, Guion's median was lower than Python's every time. The ratios run from 0.137 to 0.845.

Holds when: The frozen application suite on one Mac with CPython 3.14.7, fresh processes, outputs checked against the expected results.

Doesn't tell you: That Guion is faster at every kind of application. The smallest gain was service health, at 0.845 of Python's time. Broader task classes and carefully matched Python implementations are still needed.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-outcome-checkpoint.md https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-nine-app-comparison.json

### Does it behave the same as Python?

On the frozen application suite, Guion passed 127 of 127 cases and the independent Python version passed 127 of 127.

Holds when: Current main at commit 6b5e5aba, artifact format 44, on macOS ARM64. Every measured program output matched its expected output.

Doesn't tell you: Anything about other operating systems or CPU architectures. This checkpoint is macOS ARM64 only, and the earlier three-target cohort used an older artifact format.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-outcome-checkpoint.md https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-application-acceptance.json

### A lockfile auditor, up to 16,384 packages

Auditing 16,384 packages took Guion 171.82 ms and 40.92 MiB. Python took 179.87 ms and 47.13 MiB. Output was exact through 32,768 diagnostics.

Holds when: Seven randomized fresh-process timing pairs per size, exact-output checks, Guion's source cache bypassed, one Apple Silicon host, Python 3.14.7.

Doesn't tell you: That Guion is generally faster than Python. An earlier run of this same workload was slower than Python (1.416×); a native report serializer changed that to 0.948×. Other programs, hosts and cold-cache runs need their own measurements.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-lockfile-scale-ram-package-limit.md https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-lockfile-native-pair-serialization.json https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-lockfile-native-pair-acceptance.json https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-outcome-checkpoint.md

### A failing worker cancels its siblings

When one parallel worker fails, a sibling still waiting on an HTTP response is interrupted and its connection is closed. The original failure is the one reported.

Holds when: A local loopback test with two workers, on current main, artifact format 44, macOS ARM64. The focused test passed 1/1.

Doesn't tell you: That Guion has a general async runtime, that effects already received by a remote service are rolled back, or that this holds on Linux or other targets.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-parallel-http-cancellation.md

### Where it has been tested

An earlier cohort passed on macOS ARM64 and Debian 12 GNU/Linux on ARM64 and x86_64, all with glibc: 54 of 54 application reports. The latest speed gate ran on Linux on x86_64 and ARM64.

Holds when: For the earlier cohort: nine retained applications, initial and follow-up variants, on each of the three targets.

Doesn't tell you: Support for Windows, other Linux distributions, other CPU architectures or other C libraries. A target that did not run is reported as incomplete.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/status.md https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-10-27-current-main-outcome-checkpoint.md https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/2026-11-03-server-speed-gate.md

### When an assistant was asked to choose

In a frozen, independent exercise where assistants chose a language, they picked Python in all 18 choices for an older candidate. A later three-pair builder study recommended either language for two kinds of work and Guion's predecessor, Veritas, for one.

Holds when: These are historical studies from before the current builds, and they asked a different question from the performance results above.

Doesn't tell you: Today's recommendation. Neither study is an estimate of general adoption.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/status.md

### The name, and who it honours

Guion is named for Guion S. “Guy” Bluford Jr. On August 30, 1983, aboard Challenger on STS-8, he became the first African American to fly in space. He flew four shuttle missions and logged over 688 hours in space.

Holds when: The naming is recorded from the project's architect. The record of his flights and career comes from NASA's biographical data and NASA's article on his first flight.

Doesn't tell you: How NASA says his name. NASA confirms he goes by “Guy”; “GUY-on” is the project's own pronunciation, not a NASA record.

Evidence: https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/evidence/namesake.md
